recipes.name: Asian Chicken Salad
ingredients_raw: 1 head iceberg lettuce - rinsed, dried, and chopped
4 boneless chicken breast halves, cooked and shredded
1.5 tablespoons olive oil, or as needed

steps.text: Make the dressing: Shake oil, vinegar, brown sugar, sesame oil, and soy sauce together in a small lidded container. Set aside until salad is ready.
Make the salad: Combine lettuce, chicken, green onions, and sesame seeds in a large bowl. Cover and chill for 10 minutes.

While the salad is chilling, heat oil in a skillet over medium-low heat. Break rice noodles into pieces and fry in the hot skillet in small batches until they begin to puff up, 15 to 25 seconds. Remove to a paper towel-lined plate to drain.
Remove salad from the refrigerator. Portion into salad bowls, top with fried rice noodles, and drizzle dressing over top.

raw_recipe.headline: Asian Chicken Salad
raw_recipe.description: This Asian chicken has it all — crisp iceberg lettuce, tender chicken, crunchy fried rice noodles, and a sweet and sour sesame and soy dressing.

review.reviewBody: This is absolutely one of my favorite salad recipes! I have made this many times and tweek this depending on what I have on hand. I usually shred one carrot, add some celery, cucumber, cilantro, bean sprouts, mandarin oranges, and fresh button mushrooms. The fried noodles found in a can are easier than frying your own... or sometimes I add some slivered almonds to add a bit of crunch. Also, instead of using iceberg, I prefer to use romaine/spinach or a spring green mix. The dressing is absolutely delicious but I usually halve the amount of oil used in the recipe to make it healthier; doesn't make a difference! I've made this both with seasoned and unseasoned rice vinegar and I prefer the seasoned one in this recipe. Definitely a keeper!

Great! Here is what I did differently. For my greens I used a head of Napa cabbage and a head of romaine chopped well. I added in a lot of thickly shredded carrot, some chopped red bell pepper, chopped sugar snap peas, and cilantro. I toasted some slivered almonds and used instead of sesame seeds. I prepared the rice noodles as written because I couldn't find the prepared ones other reviewers had mentioned and don't care much for the canned chow mein noodles. I'm not sure it is worth the effort and the salad would be fine without them as long as you put almonds in for the crunch. Here is the real time saver. I bought a rotisserie chicken from Safeway and pulled the meat off the bone and shredded it up into a bowl. I doubled the recipe for the dressing, adding a bit less vegetable oil than called for, and used half of it to mix into the shredded chicken and let it sit in the fridge for a couple of hours marinating until I prepared the salad. This made the chicken taste incredible! I mixed everything together in a big bowl except the rice noodles and dressing and when we got to the pot luck I mixed it all together. Fantastic dressing recipe and you can make the salad to suit your taste. I recommend chopping everything into small pieces so you can get a little of everything in every bite.

Yum! The dressing is a dead-ringer for the ones used on Wendy's Mandarin Chicken Salad and also the asian chicken salads served at Chili's, Houston's and Panera Bread. It seriously should be printed in one of those "secret restaurant recipes revealed" cookbooks. Follow the exact recipe and you will not be disappointed. The only change I would make is...do not fry your own noodles, as suggested. It's a mess and not worth the effort. Look for pre-made fried, rice noodles (La Choy brand) in your asian food section at the grocery store. Pre-made crispy, wonton strips also work well. Also, though it's listed as "optional," you should include the sesame oil. It gives the dressing a rich, but subtle, nutty flavor. Sliced water chestnuts, a little cilantro and mandarin orange segments also add more interest to the plain salad greens.

I used pad thai rice noodles. I cut the noodles in half, fried in a 1/2 cup oil. I used olive oil instead of veggie oil, added 1 tsp of fresh chopped garlic and 1/2 tsp of ginger paste to the dressing and shook it then threw it in the fridge. That gave it the asian kick perfectly. I also shredded carrots for the salad

So I added purple cabbage, matchstick carrots, toasted slivered almonds, rotisserie chicken, mandarin oranges and romaine hearts, sesame seeds and I used angel hair rice noodles and deep fried them and they up puffed in 2 seconds, set them on a paper towel to absorb excess oil, they came out bomb! I also used less veg oil in dressing, super yummy ! My son loved this salad. Bon appetite!

This also works fine with the dried "chow mein" noodles. No frying, just throw in with the leftover cooked chicken. Lunch in about 10 minutes. I bought a case (12) of the noodles off of the internet.
I added a little rice vinegar

Just made this for dinner. We all loved it, so cool and refreshing yet filling. I just love base recipes like this that a person can expand on based on supplies on hand and personal preferance. Also love all of the ideas that everyone else shares in their reviews. Made extra dressing with 2 Tablespoons each of sesame oil and veg. oil. Lots of chopped vegetables; carrot celery cucumber, peas and Mandarin oranges. Poured some of the dressing over chopped veg, and cut up rotisseri chicken and let it set a bit then mixed with babyspinich and spring greens, oranges and toasted slivered almonds. I can't believe how fast this disappeared. It was our dinner. My daughter said "Mom don't change a thing it doesn't need to be any better, it's Great!" Thank you for sharing your recipe!!

Delicious!!! I'm on the 17 Day Diet so adapted it to meet my needs and it was still amazing! I subbed in 1 tablespoon Agave for the brown sugar. I doubled the dressing, as advised by previous reviewers, and marinated the chicken in half of it. I used the sesame oil (definitely necessary) but subbed 2 tablespoons of olive oil for the vegetable oil. I left out the rice noodles and used thinly sliced napa cabbage in place of the iceberg. A keeper recipe, for sure!

I have been searching for a great Asian sesame chicken salad recipe and this is it. Has exactly the flavor profiles I am looking for. Things I did differently: I added mandarin oranges, avocado slices, and slivered almonds. I bought wonton strip topping instead of making the rice noodles, and omitted green onion and sesame seeds. For my chicken breast, I seasoned it with salt, pepper, and garlic powder. Pan fried it in avocado oil and butter, covered for 25 min. I also halved the oil in the dressing.

I want to respond to Ellen Etc. about frying the noodles. I recogized this as being very impractical and followed the directions on the package of noodles that I bought which is to boil them. I have also found that brown rice noodles do not work well because they tend to stick together and not mix well in the salad. We like this salad so well that my husband and I have it about twice a month. It is our favorite go to meal. I have noticed that many of the pictures have mandarin oranges. They are not in the ingredient list but I will try them next time I make the salad. I also add a package of shredded carrots.

Very flavourful - added a touch of fish sauce and ginger to the dressing as per others suggestions and added mandarin oranges to the romaine /spinch mix I used. Very nice! I cooked the chicken in a wok with some chili oil (1 tbsp) and added some Ancho and Chilpolte chili powder to give it some flavor.
It was tasty. Easy to throw together also. The only thing I did differently was to substitute crushed and sautéed ramen noodles for the recipe noodles.

I only made the dressing. It was really good but too sweet for me at first taste test. So I added additional oil, vinegar and soy sauce. People said it was still too sweet so I would suggest using 1/2 amount of sugar and then increase according to your taste. I would definitely use this dressing again with the tweak. BTW, I used light brown sugar since recipe didn’t say whether to use light or dark.
Instead of using fried rice noodles, try it with stir fry udon noodles, which have more body and really only need to be warmed.
I find it annoying when the picture of the recipe does not follow the recipe. There is no tangerine in the ingredients. If it is better with the citrus then put it in the recipe to start with.
I love how simple this recipe is, but it didn't have the kick that I was hoping for. Thanks for sharing though.
When your husband looks at the plate askance and then gobbles the whole thing up - it's a winner. Wonderful variation.

Great salad but the puffed noodles were a no-go. They did puff with a little more oil but my kids said they tasted like fish bones and I agree. I will use peanuts and/or chow mein next time. I did make double dressing. I also added a daikon radish and a little carrot. Good easy salad overall.

I loved it. I did change it up using spinach and Napa cabbage I also added bean sprouts lots of shredded carrots and daikon radish toasted crushed peanuts. I had seen that others had a problem with the rice noodles I used my deep fryer and it was so easy. I also added some Thai chili peppers to both the marinade and dressing that would only work if you like heat. Thanks
The dressing really made the salad, it put it over the top
